title: The Thorn of the Glass Steppe Revisited
premise: Odile Dravenmoor, a runaway apprentice hiding in a valley where magic cannot follow, is dragged back into the world when a feral child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom. The child is a living seal, and what he seals is the thing wearing the king's crown — a parasite of the old magic that devours its hosts and rewrites their loyal memories. Odile, whose own master bound him to silence about a similar devouring years ago, must journey to the capital with the child, choosing between loyalty to the few friends who sheltered him and the truth that will shatter the realm. In the end he cannot save the king, but he can free him: Odile takes the crown's burden into himself, carries it back to the magicless valley where it starves, and the child — freed of his purpose — chooses to stay with him.
about_author: Xanthe Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing legal disputes in border towns before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whom the law was never built to protect.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Years after fleeing his master, Odile tends bees and herbs in a magicless valley, telling himself exile is peace. A child stumbles to his door at dusk, barefoot in snow, speaking words that ache to hear. The valley's stillness cracks around the boy. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, ending with the first crack in Odile's self-deception.

chapters.title: A Tongue Older Than Crowns
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with fragments from the child's perception. Odile recognizes fragments of the language from his stolen apprenticeship — it is not speech but binding, and the boy is its anchor. Hunters arrive asking after a runaway royal ward. Odile lies for the first time since fleeing. Emotional beat: the past he buried demanding interest on its silence.

chapters.title: What the Hedge-Witch Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He breaks his own rule and reads his master's stolen grimoire, learning the child is a 'living seal' and that seals are made, not born. A memory surfaces: his master binding something into a man's shadow years ago — and Odile running instead of stopping it. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve; he decides to leave the valley.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Stillness
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Odile and the child, whose chapters render the world in the seal's ancient grammar. Crossing the valley's edge, magic floods back and the boy's words begin to physically reshape the road. Odile learns the hunters serve not the crown but the thing in it. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear — magic is not his homecoming; it is the predator's territory.

chapters.title: The Loyalty of Liars
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the river-town of Marrow's Ford he reunites with Sef, a fellow runaway apprentice now thriving as an unlicensed healer. Sef offers shelter, coin, and a plan to hide the boy forever. Odile is tempted — but notices Sef flinches from the child's language. Emotional beat: warmth with a hairline fracture running through it.

chapters.title: The Crown That Eats Its Kings
chapters.summary: The child's POV, translated through Odile. The boy remembers being made: a king's firstborn, hollowed and repurposed when the parasite took the throne two reigns ago. The 'hunters' are the Royal Remembrancers, who rewrite witnesses. Odile realizes Sef has already been visited. Emotional beat: grief for a child who never got to be one, and the first open break with Sef.

chapters.title: Remembrancer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Remembrancers take Sef hostage to trade for the child. Odile goes to the exchange and learns their leader is his old master, who claims she let him escape — that his silence was her design, a seed planted against the crown-eater. He cannot tell if this is truth or another rewriting. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth tearing in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, racing the Remembrancers across the salt flats to the capital, the child weakening as the seal frays. A storm of unbound magic scours the steppe; Odile must hold the boy's language in his own mouth to keep the seal from shattering, and it begins rewriting him. Emotional beat: sacrifice made real — he is losing his own memories to carry another's truth.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax in the throne room before the crowned thing. He speaks the child's language aloud and unbinds the seal — but a seal needs a new anchor. His master offers to take it and atone; the parasite, desperate, offers Odile the king's memories as temptation. Odile binds the thing to himself instead. The king dies free; the crown falls empty. Emotional beat: terrible, clear-eyed choice.

chapters.title: Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, coda. He carries the bound parasite back across the steppe, memories thinning like frost, and re-enters the valley where it will starve. Sef, freed and changed, brings the child to him. The boy chooses a name and a home. Justice came from no court — only from a runaway who finally stopped running. Emotional beat: quiet, costly peace.
